declaration.preface:
Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG), a Reconomy Group company, recognises that ethical conduct and integrity are essential to sustainable business. In alignment with Reconomy’s group-wide strategy, we have developed this Business Ethics & Integrity Roadmap to articulate our strategic priorities and measurable commitments across anti-corruption, fraud prevention, money laundering, conflicts of interest, and information security.

This roadmap outlines how ASCG intends to advance its ethical performance, ensure legal compliance, and foster a culture of transparency, accountability, and trust.
declaration.declaration:
ASCG is committed to achieving the following general Ethics objectives:

Prevent and detect bribery, fraud, money laundering, and unethical behaviour.

Promote a culture of transparency, accountability, and lawful conduct.

Protect company and customer information from unauthorised access or misuse.

Ensure employees avoid actual or perceived conflicts of interest.

Comply with all relevant laws including the UK Bribery Act 2010 and GDPR.
declaration.scope:
This roadmap applies to all employees, stakeholders, contractors, partners, customers, contractual workers, and any individuals acting on behalf of Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG).

It covers all ASCG operational, administrative, and strategic activities across the following sites and regions:

Money Laundering Prevention: ASCG prohibits all forms of money laundering and expects employees to be alert to suspicious financial activities.
Employees must report any unusual transactions to their line manager or the Finance Director without delay.
Processing transactions known to be from illegal sources
Structuring transactions to avoid reporting requirements
Accepting cash payments above £10,000 without proper documentation
Accepting payments from high-risk jurisdictions without enhanced verification
Ignoring red flags in transaction patterns
Reporting suspicious transactions to relevant authorities
Maintaining detailed records of all financial transactions
Requesting additional documentation for unusual transactions
Training staff on money laundering indicators
Fraud Prevention: ASCG has zero tolerance for fraud. Employees must act honestly and report any suspected fraudulent activity.
All financial records must be accurate, complete, and transparent to prevent manipulation or misrepresentation.
Falsifying company documents or financial records
Deliberately concealing errors in financial statements
Manipulating financial results to meet targets
Circumventing internal controls or approval processes
Investigating minor discrepancies in financial records
Regular internal audits and compliance checks
Maintaining separation of duties for financial processes
Documentation of process exceptions with appropriate approvals
Proactive reporting of errors or mistakes
Anti-Bribery and Corruption: Offering, soliciting, or accepting bribes is strictly forbidden.
All gifts, entertainment, or hospitality exceeding £50 must be declared and approved.
All third-party relationships must be evaluated for corruption risk.
Offering, soliciting, or accepting bribes in any form
Facilitation payments to expedite routine government actions
Gifts, hospitality or entertainment exceeding £50 without approval
Providing anything of value to public officials without authorization
Using third parties to disguise corrupt payments
Donations intended to improperly influence business decisions
Modest meals with business partners (within policy limits)
Gifts of nominal value (pens, branded items, etc.)
Occasional attendance at cultural or sporting events with clear business purpose
Transparent recording of all gifts and hospitality
Legitimate charitable donations with proper approval
Proportionate hospitality that is openly documented
Conflict of Interest: Employees must disclose any personal, financial, or business interest that might conflict with ASCG’s interests.
If an employee begins a relationship with a client, supplier, or colleague in a way that may create a conflict, ASCG reserves the right to reassign roles or implement controls.
Failing to disclose personal relationships with clients or suppliers
Using company position for personal gain
Participating in decisions affecting personal financial interests
Accepting significant gifts or benefits from business partners
Using confidential information for personal advantage.
Competing with the company's business interests
Recusal from decisions involving personal connections
Obtaining approval for outside business activities
Annual declaration of interests for staff in sensitive positions
Seeking guidance from management when uncertain
Information and Cyber Security: Employees must protect sensitive information from unauthorised disclosure.
Company systems must only be accessed by authorised individuals.
Cyber security practices must be followed at all times in accordance with the Company’s Cyber Security Policy.
Sending sensitive information via unsecured channels
Downloading unauthorized software onto company devices
Discussing confidential matters in public places
Failing to report security incidents or breaches
Bypassing established security protocols or controls
Securing devices when not in use
Regular software updates and security patches
Appropriate classification and handling of sensitive data
Legitimate information sharing on a need-to-know basis
Following approved data retention and disposal procedures

targets.target: Ensure 100% of finance and procurement employees are trained annually on anti-money laundering practices by 2028.
Maintain zero substantiated internal cases of money laundering each year.
Conduct annual internal audits on expense claims and finance records at all operational sites starting 2024.
Maintain internal fraud incident rate to zero through targeted training and internal controls by 2028.
Deliver fraud awareness sessions to 100% of departments annually.
All gifts, entertainment, or hospitality exceeding £50 must be declared and approved.
Achieve 100% completion rate for anti-bribery and corruption training annually by 2028.
Ensure all gifts/hospitality above £50 are logged and reviewed within 5 working days.
Conduct corruption risk assessments on 100% of all operational sites annually.
100% of employees in management or procurement roles to submit conflict of interest declarations annually.
Respond to reported potential conflicts within 10 business days with appropriate mitigation actions.
Train 100% of its employees on conflict-of-interest topic by 2030.
Conduct biannual awareness campaigns on recognising and disclosing conflicts of interest by 2028.
Provide cyber security awareness training to 100% of system users annually by 2028.
Conduct 100% Information Security risk assessment of all operational sites annually.

responsibilities.duty: Strategic oversight of business ethics and integrity initiatives
Enforces ethical standards and ensures implementation of compliance measures
Employee training, cyber risk monitoring, ethics reporting
Oversees anti-fraud and money laundering controls
Compliance with this roadmap and timely reporting of any breach or suspicion

policy.monitoring:
Violations of the Business Ethics & Integrity Roadmap will not be tolerated. ASCG is committed to upholding the highest ethical standards, and all breaches will be investigated in line with our internal disciplinary procedures.

All reported violations will be treated confidentially and investigated impartially. Employees are encouraged to report unethical conduct in good faith and without fear of retaliation. Retaliation against whistleblowers will itself be treated as a serious disciplinary offence.

This roadmap is accessible on the ASCG intranet and provided at onboarding.

Refresher training and awareness sessions are delivered annually.
